messages:
maria: Follow-up from 2026-03-10 postmortem (missing spans + aggregation drift). Need a compact remediation plan with owners, short ETAs, and a prevention checklist. Postmortem: https://redwood.internal/postmortems/2026-03-10-spans-agg
ajay: propose we split into Detection, Fix, Restore, and Guardrails. I'll take Detection (alerts + telemetry dashboard). ETA 2d.
kevin: I can own Fix: make aggregator join null-safe and add dedupe pass. Will do migration to normalize keys in a safe window. ETA PR+staging 6d.
ella: Restore/backfill ownership: implement `spans.restore.orchestrator` with `--dry-run` and `--max-window=48h` per job, rate-limit and backoff. Dry-run 1d, phased restore 7d.
sam: Ops guardrails: daily delta ledger metric + a telemetry dashboard that shows rollup_vs_raw delta per service; add post-deploy smoke that compares top-20 service counts. Cron for sweep: `0 */6 * * *`.
lucy: I'll add a CI regression that runs a tiny synthetic corpus and fails if rollup delta > 8% for any service. Blocks merges to rollup code. ETA 3d.
audit-bot: historical-pattern-detect: matches incidents on 2025-10-12 and 2026-01-05. Recommend quarterly "rollup-health" audit.
maria: owners recap: ajay=alerts/dashboard (2d), kevin=aggregator fix+migration (6d), ella=restore orchestration (1d dry-run/7d phased), lucy=CI reg (3d), sam=ops guardrails (1d). I'll add REM-4982 and set weekly check-ins.
ajay: sample detection SQL for runbook: 
```
SELECT service, sum(case when sampled then 1 else 0 end) as sampled, count(*) as total
FROM spans
WHERE ingested_at >= now() - interval '24 hours'
GROUP BY service
HAVING (sum(case when sampled then 1 else 0 end)::float / nullif(count(*),0)) < 0.85;
```
kevin: will include before/after delta charts in PR and a rollback gate. tagging infra for migration window.
ella: will post dry-run CSV here once ready and link to REM-4982.
maria: final: i'll update the postmortem with these assignments, mark items P1, create the audit calendar, and run weekly status until closed. Ping this thread for blockers. :thumbsup:
